clue.text: She has promised to give a hand

definitions.text: She has promised to give a hand

parts.words: She has promised to give a hand
parts.note: giving one's hand means agreeing to marry, so this is a woman engaged to be wed, not a helper

explanation.surface: A woman has offered to help someone out with a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give a hand' reads as lend some help; the cryptic sense is the old phrase for accepting a marriage proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman betrothed has promised her hand in marriage, the traditional phrase for engagement.

clue.text: Total failure, if setting up a small company

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting a word up writes it bottom to top, so the word if is read backwards

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Launching a little business, if done this way, ends in complete disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiasco is a humiliating, complete collapse of an undertaking, a synonym for total failure.

clue.text: Sailor has a way with him in foreign parts

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the crossword sailor
a road is a way, a route to travel

explanation.surface: A seaman travels the world, taking his route with him to distant lands.
explanation.definitionFit: Being overseas or in another country is a synonym for being in foreign parts.

clue.text: Latin scholar makes note on ship in italics, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it, so the note comes first

parts.note: C is a musical note

indicators.note: the ship's letters are placed in the middle of the reworked letters
perhaps marks the letters of italics as only one possible arrangement, to be rearranged

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A Latinist writes a musical note next to a ship's name set in sloping type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin scholar' tempts a solver toward a Latinist; the scholar here studies the classics more broadly.
explanation.definitionFit: A classicist studies the ancient Greek and Roman world, so a Latin scholar is an example.

clue.text: More than usually wide

definitions.meaning: in cricket a wide is a ball bowled out of the batter's reach, and the run it gives is a bonus run outside the bat

explanation.surface: Something is broader than it normally is.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket counts byes, leg byes, no-balls and wides as runs not scored off the bat, all under one name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means additional, beyond the usual, and is the cricket term covering a wide.

clue.text: Fresh garb that is left for a minister of God

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters of garb are made anew in another order

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A clergyman's clothes, newly laundered, are left out for him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' rearranges GARB to GABR.
explanation.definitionFit: The archangel of the Annunciation serves as a messenger of God, one of his ministering angels.

clue.text: Fruit stolen and used as missiles?

parts.note: grapes are a fruit
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: Pinched fruit gets thrown at people.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: small iron balls fired in clusters from a cannon, the question mark admitting the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: This old artillery load was clusters of small balls fired from cannon as projectiles.

clue.text: Brought up with money, by the sound of it

indicators.note: these words say that the slang word for money is heard, and a word spelt differently but pronounced the same is written in

parts.note: bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone was raised in a wealthy family, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: To be raised by one's parents is a synonym for having been brought up.

clue.text: Man rises above this environment

parts.note: Man is the Isle of Man, which stands up out of the stretch of water around it

explanation.surface: Humanity triumphs over its surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' reads as humankind, but it is the island between Britain and Ireland, set in the sea named after Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man lies in the waters between Great Britain and Ireland, its surrounding sea.

clue.text: Flag and sail hung incorrectly

indicators.note: something done incorrectly is wrongly arranged, so these letters must be put in another order

explanation.surface: A flag and a sail have been hoisted the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' is a verb here, to droop or weaken, not a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to tire and droop, a synonym for pining or wasting away.

clue.text: A new rota for building a large vessel

indicators.note: a new version of the word rota means its letters in a different order

explanation.surface: A fresh duty roster is drawn up for constructing a big ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges ROTA to ORTA. 'Vessel' suggests a ship; here it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The main artery leaving the heart is the body's largest blood vessel.

clue.text: Train crash included elderly actor

indicators.note: the word for elderly is put inside the jumbled letters
a train crash leaves the carriages scattered, so the letters of train are jumbled

parts.note: aged means elderly

explanation.surface: An old actor was among those caught up in a railway accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'actor' is narrowed: a tragedian specialises in tragic roles.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer specialising in serious dramatic roles is a kind of actor.

clue.text: Superior teams, oddly, are those that learn together

parts.note: class as an adjective means top-quality, superior

indicators.note: oddly signals the letters of teams are arranged strangely

explanation.surface: Top sides, strangely, are the ones that practise as one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' rearranges TEAMS to MATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils in the same school form are fellow students who are taught side by side.

clue.text: You used to be grand

definitions.meaning: the archaic singular form of you, as in older English and the Bible
a grand is a thousand pounds or dollars, shortened in slang

explanation.surface: Someone is told they were once magnificent.
explanation.definitionFit: The old word for you, and slang for a thousand, as in a grand.

clue.text: A subject for those who have a mind to study

definitions.text: A subject for those who have a mind to study

parts.words: A subject for those who have a mind to study
parts.note: having a mind to study reads as being keen to learn, but cryptically means wanting to study the mind itself

explanation.surface: A school subject suited to anyone willing to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have a mind to' means be inclined to; the trick is reading 'a mind' as the thing being studied.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical field dealing with mental illness takes the human mind as its subject.

clue.text: Line clippers?

parts.note: clippers suggests a tool for trimming, but these clip washing onto a washing line

explanation.surface: Tools for trimming a line or edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clippers' suggests shears; here things clip on to a line rather than cut it.
explanation.definitionFit: Small wooden or plastic clips hold laundry onto a washing line, so they clip on to a line.

clue.text: Different white and rosé, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the wine names are only a possible arrangement of letters to be reordered

explanation.surface: The two wine colours are distinct, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means in another way or of another kind, a synonym for different.

clue.text: View of both parents about Nora

indicators.note: the parents' names sit around Nora, one on each side

parts.note: the two parents are pa and ma, father and mother, written side by side

explanation.surface: Mum and Dad's opinion of Nora.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide unbroken vista across a landscape is a sweeping view.

clue.text: What may be seen, when scurvy knaves are collared

definitions.text: What may be seen, when scurvy knaves are collared

parts.words: What may be seen, when scurvy knaves are collared
parts.note: scurvy means scurfy, flaky-scalped, and the flakes show up on the collar of a jacket

explanation.surface: A scene of villains being arrested, pirate style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scurvy knaves' and 'collared' suggest rogues seized; read literally, scurvy is scurfy and the collar is where scalp flakes land.
explanation.definitionFit: Flakes of dead skin from the scalp fall onto the shoulders and collars of the scurfy.

clue.text: Number employed in the theatre

parts.note: number reads as a song in a show, but it is something that numbs, used in an operating theatre

explanation.surface: A song performed on stage in a musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is numb-er, a thing that numbs, and the theatre is a hospital operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug that removes sensation, used before surgery, numbs the patient.

clue.text: Mounted plate displaying a horse, say

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means climbing upward, so the word for plate is read from the bottom

parts.note: a lamina is a thin plate or layer

explanation.surface: A wall plaque shows a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounted' sends LAMINA upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse is one example of a living creature, signalled by say.

clue.text: Note record of people influential in society

parts.note: G is a musical note
an entry is a record made in a log or ledger

explanation.surface: A list noting who the movers and shakers are.
explanation.definitionFit: The landed upper classes, just below the nobility, were the well-born people who held sway socially.

clue.text: They give better prices

parts.note: better reads as superior, but a better here is one who bets, and the prices are what a bookmaker offers

explanation.surface: Some shops offer cheaper deals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is bet-ter, a gambler.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookmaker's quoted prices tell a punter what a winning bet will pay.

clue.text: Talent that outshines all others

parts.note: outshines puns on shining light, so the gift is one of dazzling brightness

explanation.surface: An outstanding gift beats every rival.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means both exceptional talent and intense brightness, which 'outshines' plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Exceptional cleverness or skill, and also dazzling radiance, which outshines everything.

clue.text: Socially one left right out

indicators.note: the left and right letters stand outside, one at each end, with one inside them

explanation.surface: Someone who has been completely shut out of social life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' has L and R on the outside of ONE. Read whole, the clue also describes the answer: a person left right out socially.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitary person who avoids company is one cut off from others socially.

clue.text: Writer destined for the chop?

definitions.meaning: Charles ... was an English essayist, author of Essays of Elia
a young sheep raised for meat ends up as chops

explanation.surface: An author is about to be sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the chop' reads as dismissal; here it is a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: The essayist Charles Lamb, and the young sheep whose meat is sold as chops.

clue.text: To laud in a way that's flattering

definitions.note: read as a noun phrase, something that's flattering, i.e. excessive praise

indicators.note: in a way here means differently arranged, so the letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: Praising someone in a particular manner flatters them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way' (as in 'in a way') rearranges TO LAUD IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive admiration or fawning praise is flattery, what flatters its target.

clue.text: Invite agency worker to try, initially

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker placed by an agency

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the word try

explanation.surface: Ask a temporary employee to have a go, to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure or entice someone is to invite them toward something; a synonym.

clue.text: Football federation recalled legendary tale that's friendly

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the two letters are read in reverse

parts.note: the FA is England's Football Association
a fable is a legendary or moral tale

explanation.surface: A football body brings back a cheerful old story.
explanation.definitionFit: Good-natured and easy to talk to is a synonym of friendly.

clue.text: Payment to an author — it isn't common

definitions.meaning: a share of each sale paid to a writer
commoners are the ordinary people, so royals are not common

explanation.surface: A writer's fee is unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer's per-copy fee, and the kings and queens who are anything but commoners.
